## Stable

Covered by the compatibility promise in [VERSIONING.md](../VERSIONING.md): an incompatible change to the exported Go API is preceded by a deprecation window.

### analytics

- `public/analytics/stats/letterval` — Package letterval computes letter-value summaries (Hofmann, Wickham & Kafadar 2017) from any source that can answer Quantile/CDF queries.
- `public/analytics/stats/tdigest` — Package tdigest provides a streaming quantile sketch with tail-biased accuracy, based on Dunning 2019 (arXiv:1902.04023).

### caching

- `public/caching` — Package caching is a read-through cache for work that can be suspended and replayed — ETL steps, build graphs, traversals — where fetching is expensive and computing is cheap.

### config

- `public/config/env` — Package env is the boxer-wide environment variable registry.
- `public/config/env/envcli` — Package envcli derives urfave/cli flags and the `env` command from the variables registered with public/config/env.
- `public/config/env/envtest` — Package envtest sets registry variables from tests.

### containers

- `public/containers` — Package containers holds small generic in-memory containers:
- `public/containers/co` — Package co provides operations over co-indexed parallel slices — separate slices whose elements correspond by position (a struct-of-arrays layout): sorting a lead slice while keeping companions aligned (CoSortSlices), sorted insertion and merge over a key slice plus a value slice, grouped iteration over key runs, and co-filtered iteration.
- `public/containers/ragged` — Package ragged provides zip iterators that tolerate length-mismatched ("ragged") inputs by stopping at the shorter side: [Zip2] for two slices, and [Zip2L], [Zip2R], [Zip2LR] where the suffix letters mark which operand positions are lazy (iter.Seq-valued).

### db

- `public/db/clickhouse/chrows` — Package chrows reads a ClickHouse Arrow result into Go values (ADR-0257): per-cell readers that absorb the several Arrow spellings one ClickHouse type arrives in, and [Decode] / [DecodeStream], which lay a whole result into a struct of column slices tagged `ch:"<column>"`.
- `public/db/clickhouse/chtype` — Package chtype parses ClickHouse type strings into a small syntax tree.
- `public/db/clickhouse/dsl/sqlvocab` — Package sqlvocab is the shared shape a SQL vocabulary roster declares itself in: a function's name, its parameters in order, and — the part that is new — what each parameter *is* (ADR-0190 §SD4).
- `public/db/clickhouse/logcomment` — Package logcomment is the one wire format of the identity stamp boxer clients put in ClickHouse's log_comment setting (ADR-0115 §SD7, ADR-0295 §SD2).

### extbin

- `public/extbin` — Package extbin is boxer's single sanctioned entry point for invoking external programs.

### functional

- `public/functional` — Package functional holds small generic helpers over iterators and values: projecting and swapping iter.Seq2 pairs ([IterLeftOnly], [IterRightOnly], [IterInterchanged]), lifting an iter.Seq into an iter.Seq2 ([MakeIter2FromIter1], [MakeIter2FromIter1Indexed]), one-value iterators, [TranslateEmpty], and [NilIteratorValueType], the element type of an iterator used only as a scope (`for range x.KeepIter()`).
- `public/functional/option` — Package option provides a typed Some/None carrier for fields that may be present or absent.

### identity

- `public/identity/callident` — Package callident carries who a call is made for on its context (ADR-0295 §SD1): the run, app and window the host vouches for, and the principal, purpose and correlation the caller states.
- `public/identity/fibonacci` — Package fibonacci is the tag-planning layer over the fibonacci-coded identifier scheme (ADR-0106 SD4): given how many ids a category must hold, or how wide a code it may spend, it answers which tag values qualify.
- `public/identity/fibonaccicode` — Package fibonaccicode encodes and decodes Fibonacci codes (Zeckendorf representations terminated by a "11" comma) in a uint64, MSB-aligned.
- `public/identity/identifier` — Package identifier defines boxer's 64-bit tagged ids: a [TaggedId] is a tag ([IdTag]) in the high bits followed by an id body ([UntaggedId]) in the rest.
- `public/identity/tagmint` — Package tagmint is the authority for identifier tag values: the one place a tag value is claimed, and the only source of the token the registries that mint tagged ids demand.

### keelson

- `public/keelson/designsystem/styletokens` — Package styletokens is the Go-side mirror of the IDS token layer (Rust source-of-truth at src/rust/imzero2_egui/src/style/tokens/).
- `public/keelson/runtime/app` — Package app is the runtime's first-class app abstraction.
- `public/keelson/runtime/appops` — Package appops is how an app declares its operations catalog (ADR-0269 §SD2) and the handlers behind it in one place.
- `public/keelson/runtime/codec/kindcheck` — Package kindcheck answers "do these facts-CBOR bytes claim kind K?" for hosts that must validate a payload at a boundary without importing the payload's Go type (ADR-0135 §SD1: the window host refuses a malformed or mistargeted launch config before the target app sees it).
- `public/keelson/runtime/icons` — Package icons supplies the IDS iconography catalogue.
- `public/keelson/runtime/lifetime` — Package lifetime groups work that is retired as one, and lets the owner wait for it to finish (ADR-0322).
- `public/keelson/runtime/persist` — Package persist implements the ADR-0026 §SD3 runtime.persist.{alias}.{key}.{op} subject family.
- `public/keelson/runtime/task` — Package task is keelson's bus-protocol primitive for long-running, cancellable, observable work — the M1 surface of ADR-0038.

### math

- `public/math/numerical/timeticks` — Package timeticks generates calendar-aware tick layouts for time axes.

### observability

- `public/observability/eh` — Package eh builds errors that carry the stack of the call site and, optionally, structured data, and reads them back for logs and records.
- `public/observability/eh/eb` — Package eb is the builder that attaches structured fields to an error:
- `public/observability/ph` — Package ph turns a recovered panic into an error, and holds the panic boundaries a runtime-owned entry point is built from (ADR-0386).

### semistructured

- `public/semistructured/cbor/buscodec` — Package buscodec is the runtime's canonical message-bus codec (ADR-0036).
- `public/semistructured/cbor/diag` — Package diag renders CBOR bytes as RFC 8949 §8 diagnostic notation — ADR-0219 §SD6: the pretty-printer under the cbordiag widget and the `cbor diagnostics --pretty` CLI.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/dml/runtime` — Package runtime is the support code leeway-generated write sides import: the interfaces a generated attribute and membership builder implement (one per membership channel), the error-accumulating contract ([ErrorHandlingI]), helpers such as [AppendFixedText], and [DeferredSectionBuffer], which lets several typed contributions to one entity be emitted section by section in a fixed order.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/marshall/clickhouse/componentsql` — Package componentsql publishes the ADR-0066 read-back artefacts a component definition generates, and the registry a SQL-authoring surface looks them up in (ADR-0189).
- `public/semistructured/leeway/membership` — Package membership is the low-level wire identity of a Leeway membership and its string representation, role-agnostic.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/naming` — Package naming is the vocabulary of names in a leeway schema: a [StylableName] (a table, section or column name that converts between naming styles without losing what it refers to) and a [Key] (an identifier used as is, such as a streaming or co-section group).
- `public/semistructured/leeway/readaccess/runtime` — Package runtime is the support code leeway-generated read sides import: the interfaces generated readers implement ([ColumnIndexHandlingI], [SectionMethodsI], one InAttributeMembership…I per membership channel), the index types ([EntityIdx], [AttributeIdx]) and the lookup accelerators that map an entity to its attributes in a loaded record.
- `public/semistructured/markdown/obsidian/ext/blockid` — Package blockid parses Obsidian block identifiers (ADR-0347 §SD4): a trailing ` ^id` on the last line of a block names that block, so a link `[[note#^id]]` can reach it.

### storage

- `public/storage/recordstore` — Package recordstore is the runtime support layer for generated leeway record stores (ADR-0100).

### thestack

- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/bindings` — Package bindings holds the Go-side fluent builders for egui2 widgets, blocks, and plots — a mix of code generated by egui2gen (the .out.go / .gen.go files) and hand-written companions that compose those primitives into higher-level surfaces (badges, code views, graph integration, etc.).
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/badge` — Package badge implements a compact labelled tag rendered as a Frame (rounded fill + optional stroke + padding) wrapping a styled LabelAtoms.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/bandscale` — Package bandscale is an immediate-mode widget (ADR-0267) that draws a linear scale of named bands with markers on it: an ordinal ladder — severity, authority, readiness — where a position is judged against the band it falls in.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/bowtie` — Package bowtie draws a bow-tie diagram, a semi-retained widget (ADR-0267): threats on the left, the prevention barriers each must pass in series, one top event in the centre, the mitigation barriers in series after it, and the consequences on the right.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/breadcrumbs` — Package breadcrumbs is an immediate-mode widget (ADR-0267) that draws a trail of items in one row, separated by a caret: the segments of a path, or the steps of a wizard.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/cardgrid` — Package cardgrid is an imzero2 widget that renders a page of items as a responsive grid of uniform cards — hero, overline, title, subtitle, body, facts, tags, footer.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/cbordiag` — Package cbordiag is an immediate-mode widget (ADR-0267) that shows CBOR bytes as RFC 8949 §8 diagnostic notation — ADR-0219 §SD6: a toolbar (byte count, a compact / expanded toggle, a copy button, an optional verdict line the host sets) over a codeview job built from the cbor/diag printer's spans.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/chatview` — Package chatview is an imzero2 widget that renders a conversation — a sequence of timestamped, attributed messages — as a transcript of bubbles: a two-party dialogue laid out like a phone's SMS view (the viewer's messages on the right, the other party's on the left), or a group chat (every message on the left under its sender's name and colour, the viewer's on the right), or a thread (every message a full-width block from the left edge, the viewer's tinted — for long bodies, and with nothing right-aligned to measure).
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/colorscale` — Package colorscale renders a value-axis legend for a colormap.Config — the same colormap type the scientific texture widgets (heatmapscroll) and treemap use.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/console` — Package console is a terminal screen: a semi-retained widget (ADR-0267) over the client's console opcode, decided in ADR-0359.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/editexternally` — Package editexternally draws the gesture that hands a window's text to the host's editor app and brings each save back (externaledit): one button while idle, and while the text is handed over the edit's status, a way to stop, and the choice when a save arrives after the person edited the text here.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/errorview` — Package errorview is an immediate-mode widget (ADR-0267) that renders a structured wrapped-error chain as a collapsing tree: per-stream sub-headers, per-fact rows showing message (red), stack frame triple (monospace muted), and CBOR diagnostic of any attached structured data (in a dark canvas Frame).
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/fieldview` — Package fieldview is an immediate-mode widget (ADR-0267) that renders a hierarchical list of typed key-value pairs as an outline: one row per field, name and kind tag in the first column and the value (monospace) in the second.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/fsmview` — Package fsmview is a semi-retained imzero2 widget (ADR-0267): a two-level finite-state-machine viewer.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/gauge` — Package gauge is an immediate-mode widget (ADR-0267) that renders a read-only radial dial: one scalar value mapped onto a bounded [min,max] range, drawn as a ~270° needle dial with optional colored zones, ticks, and a center value readout.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/graphview` — Package graphview is the live node-and-edge graph widget of ADR-0224: random, force-directed (Fruchterman–Reingold, optionally with centre gravity) and hierarchical layouts, drawn on the imzero2 painter lane with no IDL, Rust or fetcher of its own.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/graphview/nav` — Package nav is the navigation layer above graphview (ADR-0225): a universe of nodes and edges the caller feeds, a small navigation state — roots, expansions, hidden nodes, a focus list — and the declaration graphview renders, derived from the two.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/heatmapscroll` — Package heatmapscroll composes the colormap package with the scrollingTexture widget (ADR-0058) into a single, opinionated wrapper for "streaming scalar → colour heatmap" use cases: audio spectrograms, RF waterfalls, thermal streams, rolling metrics heatmaps.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/markdown` — Package markdown is an immediate-mode widget (ADR-0267) over a parsed Doc: it renders Obsidian-flavored Markdown documents through the imzero2 / egui2 widget tree.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/mdblocks` — Package mdblocks is a semi-retained widget (ADR-0267) that edits a markdown document as a vertical list of blocks over the one source string — the shape ADR-0334 decided.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/mdoutline` — Package mdoutline is the heading outline of a markdown document: the hierarchy a document's headings make, nested by level, drawn through the native tree widget with a section that folds away, a selection that follows the reader's position and a reveal that opens the way to it.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/pager` — Package pager is a semi-retained imzero2 widget (ADR-0267): a client-side paginator over an in-memory dataset.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/portolan` — Package portolan is the slippy-map widget's kernel: a Go port of the map core of Leaflet (https://github.com/Leaflet/Leaflet — BSD-2-Clause, © 2010–2026 Volodymyr Agafonkin, © 2010–2011 CloudMade), taken from upstream main at commit c96f31a7a350a07cfbc852cf88e6ca69af5f5ec9 (the 2.0.0-alpha.1 line) and re-targeted onto the imzero2 painter lane (ADR-0204).
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/portolan/landoverlay` — Package landoverlay draws the world's landmasses and country borders on a portolan map from the worldmap atlas — the vendored Natural Earth 110m admin-0 outlines — through the projector hook, so a map with no tile server still shows geography (ADR-0204 §SD9's pattern, as h3overlay follows it).
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/regexedit` — Package regexedit is the syntax-highlighted regex input, extracted from the regex_explorer demo app for reuse by the battery search boxes (ADR-0164 §SD4).
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/runtimestatus` — Package runtimestatus is an immediate-mode widget (ADR-0267) rendering a one-line snapshot of the active runtime services for the host chrome's bottom panel.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/selector` — Package selector renders an "exactly one of N" choice bound directly to a Go enum value, filling the gap left by the egui2 bindings: egui's own enum-native helpers — `Ui::radio_value(&mut current, value, text)` and `Ui::selectable_value(...)`, whose whole point is to compare-and-assign an enum in one call — are not exposed in the IDL.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/spectrumdisplay` — Package spectrumdisplay renders a spectrum-analyzer display: a scrolling waterfall with a labelled frequency axis (engineering Hz/kHz/MHz units), a power/dB colorbar legend, an optional spectrum-line trace, frequency/time annotations (markers and named regions), and a cursor readout in physical units.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/timeline` — Package timeline is a semi-retained widget (ADR-0267) for interval events on a calendar axis.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/timescrubber` — Package timescrubber is a time strip for a stepped series — forecast steps, snapshots, frames — drawn on the painter lane (ADR-0251): a control that shows where in time there is something to look at, and what moving there will cost, before the reader moves.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/tree` — Package tree renders a hierarchy as an outline: one row per visible node, indented by depth, with a disclosure control on any node that has children (ADR-0176).
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/treemap` — Package treemap is a semi-retained widget (ADR-0267): an interactive Frame-based treemap with zoom-from-rect transitions on drill-in and drill-up.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/videooutput` — Package videooutput is the ADR-0088 "video output" control for the imzero2 remote-stream pipeline, an immediate-mode widget (ADR-0267) in two parts:
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/worldmap` — Package worldmap renders a schematic world choropleth: countries from the embedded Natural Earth 110m admin-0 asset, filled by a per-country value through a colormap, drawn Go-side into a content-versioned texture (ADR-0114).

## Experimental

Public and usable, but may change in any MINOR version without a deprecation window.

### algebraicarch

- `public/algebraicarch/pushout/envelope` — Package envelope defines the transmissible form of a patch and its wire-format seam.
- `public/algebraicarch/pushout/exchange` — Version comparison.
- `public/algebraicarch/pushout/exchange/inproc` — Package inproc adapts a local *repo.Repo to the exchange transport interfaces — the trivial carrier used by the demo, by tests, and by the exchangetest conformance suite.
- `public/algebraicarch/pushout/pushoutgraph/algo` — Package algo provides pure graph algorithms operating on the GraphReaderI interface.
- `public/algebraicarch/pushout/pushoutgraph/dot` — Package dot provides Graphviz DOT format export for pushoutgraph graphs.
- `public/algebraicarch/pushout/pushoutgraph/patch` — Package patch provides patch construction, application, and dependency tracking for the pushout revision control system.
- `public/algebraicarch/pushout/pushoutgraph/qc` — Package qc provides structural invariant checking for pushoutgraph graphs.
- `public/algebraicarch/pushout/pushoutgraph/store` — Package store provides the concrete PushoutGraph data structure implementing all graph interfaces defined in the types package.
- `public/algebraicarch/pushout/pushoutgraph/types` — Package types defines the core data types and interfaces for the pushout revision control system.
- `public/algebraicarch/pushout/repo` — Package repo is the domain-neutral pushout engine: a patch log plus a pushoutgraph, persisted through a pluggable [StorageI], serialized through a pluggable wire-codec [envelope.Registry], and synchronized through the transport-agnostic exchange package.
- `public/algebraicarch/pushout/repo/filestore` — Package filestore is the reference [repo.StorageI] implementation: a transparent on-disk layout under one root directory, hardened for crash consistency.

### analytics

- `public/analytics/explain` — Package explain reads a labelling back off the feature matrix it was made from (ADR-0235): given a row-major matrix and a label per row, it fits a threshold tree to the labels and measures, per label and feature, how the members' values sit against everyone else's.
- `public/analytics/graph/algo` — Package algo holds the whole-graph metrics of the graph analytics engine (ADR-0229 §SD3): degrees, breadth-first distances, connected and strongly connected components, PageRank, k-core decomposition, triangle counting, betweenness centrality and maximal cliques — and, over a distance-weighted graph, HDBSCAN (ADR-0230 §SD3).
- `public/analytics/graph/csr` — Package csr is the one adjacency container of the graph analytics engine (ADR-0229 §SD1): vertex ids mapped to dense slots, forward and reverse adjacency as offset and target arrays, neighbours sorted by id within each row, built once per topology by counting sort.
- `public/analytics/graph/engine` — Package engine is the iteration layer of the graph analytics engine (ADR-0229 §SD2): a frontier ([Subset]) kept sparse or dense, an edge map whose direction is chosen per sweep, and chunked parallelism whose result is bit-identical to the serial one.
- `public/analytics/graph/knn` — Package knn is the neighbour-graph producer of the graph analytics engine (ADR-0230 §SD1): a feature matrix in, a weighted undirected github.com/stergiotis/boxer/public/analytics/graph/csr.Graph out.
- `public/analytics/graph/rutter` — Package rutter is the road-network routing engine (ADR-0256): a graph of arcs with identities, a metric as a column over them, Dijkstra as the oracle, an Inertial Flow nested-dissection order, a Customizable Contraction Hierarchy with basic customization and an elimination-tree query, many-to-many by buckets, and a grid index for snapping a point to the nearest polyline.
- `public/analytics/similarity/compression`
- `public/analytics/similarity/compression/stylometry`
- `public/analytics/stats`
- `public/analytics/stats/distsql` — Package distsql implements the ADR-0161 distribution result contract: the fixed probability grid the descriptiveStatistics macro emits, the claim validation rules the play Distribution panel applies, and the letterval.QuantileOracle adapter that feeds a boxenplot ladder from a server-side quantile grid.
- `public/analytics/stats/ecdfbands` — Package ecdfbands implements finite-sample exact simultaneous confidence bands on the empirical cumulative distribution function of an iid univariate sample.
- `public/analytics/stats/ecdfbands/digest` — Package digest bridges a tdigest.TDigest to the ecdfbands library.
- `public/analytics/timeseries/adscore` — Package adscore scores time-series anomaly detectors against labelled data, and generates labelled fixtures that are worth scoring against.
- `public/analytics/timeseries/changepoint` — Package changepoint finds the positions at which a series changes regime: its level, or its level and spread, is one thing up to a sample and another from the next.
- `public/analytics/timeseries/damp` — Package damp finds left discords over an arriving stream: subsequences whose nearest neighbour among everything that came *before* them is far away.
- `public/analytics/timeseries/loadstudy` (integration-test) — Package loadstudy pulls real recorded load metrics and application events out of ClickHouse so the ADR-0150 detectors can be measured against something nobody synthesised.
- `public/analytics/timeseries/matrixprofile` — Package matrixprofile computes the matrix profile of a real-valued time series: for every subsequence of a fixed length, the z-normalized Euclidean distance to its nearest non-trivial neighbour, and that neighbour's index.
- `public/analytics/timeseries/mssmooth` — Package mssmooth smooths equidistant series by convolution with a modified-sinc (MS) kernel — the Savitzky–Golay replacement of Schmid, Rath and Diebold, ACS Meas.

### apps

- `apps/fibscope/launchcfg` — Package launchcfg is fibscope's launch configuration (keelson-app S4): the leeway-declared DTO a launch request may carry (ADR-0135) — the id a window opens on, so another app can show how one of its ids splits without importing the app and its registering init().
- `apps/mdedit/launchcfg` — Package launchcfg is mdedit's launch configuration (ADR-0178, update of 2026-10-03): the leeway-declared DTO a launch request may carry (ADR-0135) — a document another app hands over, opened as a document of its own beside the one mdedit keeps.
- `apps/mdedit/mdeditlink` — Package mdeditlink is the `mdedit://` link (ADR-0347): the one string that names a document in a lading snapshot, a place in it and the view mode to show it in, and the one way every app follows it — a launch request for a new mdedit window.
- `apps/notebook/launchcfg` — Package launchcfg is the notebook window's launch configuration (ADR-0371 §SD10): the leeway-declared DTO a launch request may carry (ADR-0135) — a notebook another app hands over.
- `apps/play/launchcfg` — Package launchcfg holds play's own app id and re-exports the playground's launch contract, which moved to public/keelson/runtime/playground (ADR-0361 §SD4).
- `apps/sqlappletcreator/appletcreatecfg` — Package appletcreatecfg is the launch contract of the SQL applet creator (ADR-0132 Update "O4" / ADR-0135 §SD7): the target app id, the config kind, and the typed arguments an app opens a creator window with over `windowhost.open`.
- `apps/tally/launchcfg` — Package launchcfg is tally's launch configuration (ADR-0200 §SD9): the leeway-declared DTO a launch request may carry (ADR-0135) and a workingset restores (ADR-0148) — the two panes' locations, the synchronized-browsing flag and the target pane.
- `apps/terrainscope/launchcfg` — Package launchcfg is terrainscope's launch configuration (keelson-app S4): the leeway-declared DTO a launch request may carry (ADR-0135) — the two points a window opens on, so another app can ask for a line-of-sight sweep without importing the app and its registering init().
- `apps/watchbill/launchcfg` — Package launchcfg is the watchbill management app's launch configuration (ADR-0236 §SD4): the leeway-declared DTO a launch request may carry (ADR-0135) — one job to show, or a filter to open on.
- `apps/writingstylescope/launchcfg` — Package launchcfg is writingstylescope's launch configuration (keelson-app S4): the leeway-declared DTO a launch request may carry (ADR-0135) — the two documents a window opens on and the section-length floor, so another app can ask for a comparison without importing the app and its registering init().

### db

- `public/db/badger`
- `public/db/clickhouse/chhttp` — Package chhttp implements the server side of the ClickHouse HTTP dialect (ADR-0133 §SD1): what an in-process endpoint needs to answer HTTP like a ClickHouse server, closely enough for clients written against the real one (apps/play posts a statement and reads an ArrowStream back).
- `public/db/clickhouse/clickhouseenv` — Package clickhouseenv centralises the ClickHouse-related environment variables consumed across boxer: the funccharacterize fuzzer, the play HMI, and the live test harness.
- `public/db/clickhouse/dsl/grammar1` — Package grammar1 is the ANTLR-generated lexer and parser for ClickHouse SQL that nanopass.Parse uses: the permissive grammar, which accepts the spellings people write.
- `public/db/clickhouse/dsl/grammar2`
- `public/db/clickhouse/dsl/marshalling` — Package marshalling converts between Go values and ClickHouse SQL literal text: scalars, homogeneous arrays and tuples, as a [TypedLiteral] that keeps the canonical type beside the value so a literal round-trips without losing its type.
- `public/db/clickhouse/dsl/nanopass` — Package nanopass is the framework for rewriting ClickHouse SQL as a sequence of small passes, each taking SQL text and returning SQL text.
- `public/db/clickhouse/dsl/nanopass/analysis` — Package analysis answers read-only questions about a parsed ClickHouse statement: which tables, columns and functions it references ([ExtractTables], [ExtractColumns], [ExtractFunctions]), what kind of statement it is ([ClassifyStatementKind], [Classify]), which stratum a query falls in ([ClassifyQueryStratum]) and what it can reach ([ClassifyQuerySecurity]).
- `public/db/clickhouse/dsl/nanopass/nanopasstest` — Package nanopasstest checks a nanopass pass's declared properties from a test.
- `public/db/clickhouse/dsl/nanopass/passes` — Package passes holds the SQL-to-SQL passes built on github.com/stergiotis/boxer/public/db/clickhouse/dsl/nanopass: the canonicalize family that brings a statement into the function-call form later passes expect ([CanonicalizeFull] composes them into one pass), and rewrites such as [QualifyTables], [ExtractLiterals] with [InjectParams], [SetFormat], [StripComments], [ValidateColumnNames] and [ResolveColumnNames].
- `public/db/clickhouse/dsl/sqlcomplete` — Package sqlcomplete answers "what may stand where the caret is" for a ClickHouse buffer (ADR-0190).
- `public/db/clickhouse/jackstay` — Package jackstay is the engine of the guided ClickHouse-to-ClickHouse sync of ADR-0259.
- `public/db/fairlead` — Package fairlead is the one opening every SQL statement passes on its way out of the process (ADR-0367 §SD1).

### fs

- `public/fs/lading` — Package lading is the fs snapshot store (ADR-0198): a walk of an `fs.FS` is written once as a snapshot into facts-shaped ClickHouse tables the store controls — never updated, never shared, retained by TTL — and read back through a snapshot-pinned `io/fs` adapter or queried as SQL.
- `public/fs/lading/ladingadapter` — Package ladingadapter turns one snapshot of one mount into an `io/fs.FS` (ADR-0198 §SD8).
- `public/fs/lading/ladingadhoc` — Package ladingadhoc publishes an in-memory file tree as a short-lived lading mount (ADR-0222 §SD5).
- `public/fs/lading/ladingdata`
- `public/fs/lading/ladingingest` — Package ladingingest walks an `fs.FS` and writes it into the lading store as one snapshot (ADR-0198 §SD5, §SD6).
- `public/fs/lading/ladingmeta`
- `public/fs/lading/ladingpolicy`
- `public/fs/lading/ladingremote` — Package ladingremote presents an SFTP connection as an `io/fs.FS`, and spawns `rclone serve sftp --stdio <remote>` to get one (ADR-0198 §SD9).
- `public/fs/lading/ladingschema` — Package ladingschema holds what the lading store's three tables are — their names, their leeway shape, their engine clauses and the ALTERs and materialised view that finish them (ADR-0198 §SD2, §SD4).
- `public/fs/lading/ladingsftp` — Package ladingsftp serves a lading store over SFTP on a pipe (ADR-0198 §SD9).
- `public/fs/lading/ladingsftp/sftptree` — Package sftptree names the tree the lading SFTP head serves (ADR-0198 §SD9): a mount's directory, a snapshot's directory, and the rclone remote that reaches one.
- `public/fs/lading/ladingsql` — Package ladingsql is the SQL surface of the lading store (ADR-0198 §SD7): three table-function macros that turn a mount id into a readable relation.
- `public/fs/lading/ladingview` — Package ladingview is what an interactive host needs around an adapter view (ADR-0200 §SD4): the locking wrapper that lets one render thread and several lanes share the single-goroutine stores (ADR-0100), and the bounded read a preview wants — a file's head, its size and its kind in one call.
- `public/fs/lading/ladingvocab` — Package ladingvocab is the lading store's leeway natural-key vocabulary: the memberships that tag a file-tree row in the store's own facts-shaped tables, and the mount policy record in `boxer.facts` (ADR-0198 §SD2).

### hmi

- `public/hmi/gloss` — Package gloss is the core of ADR-0186: a catalog of glosses — named ways of showing a value — that a host such as play resolves per result column and renders in a table cell (the inline face) or a detail pane (a block face the host binds by media type).
- `public/hmi/gloss/glosssql` — Package glosssql is the gloss(…) constructor macro of ADR-0186 §SD7: a client-side nanopass expansion pass, in the shape of ADR-0181's LwConstructExpand, that turns
- `public/hmi/progressbar`
- `public/hmi/progressest` — Package progressest is boxer's one estimator of how fast a job runs and when it will finish: Holt's double exponential smoothing over the job's counter, with a damping layer on the displayed ETA, plus the duration, ETA, byte and rate spellings every progress readout shares.

### identity

- `public/identity/identgen` — Package identgen groups the concrete identifier.IdGeneratorI implementations — seq/ (per-tag monotonic counters) and internalized/ (natural-key interners), each with an in-memory and a Badger backend — and the errors they share.
- `public/identity/identgen/leased` — Package leased generates identifier.IdGeneratorI ids over a technology-neutral identgen.AllocatorI: the id source is a swappable block allocator rather than a hard-wired embedded store.
- `public/identity/identgen/leased/memalloc` — Package memalloc is an in-memory identgen.AllocatorI: a per-tag monotonic counter handing out body-value blocks.
- `public/identity/identgen/leased/rowalloc` — Package rowalloc is an identgen.AllocatorI over one lease row per tag on the one ClickHouse server a deployment runs (ADR-0319 §SD1, §SD3): the row carries the next unleased body, and a block is reserved by a compare-and-set on it — a guarded lightweight update writing the new bound and a holder token, then a read of the row by the same client.
- `public/identity/identgen/mem` — Package mem is the dependency-free, in-memory get-or-assign identifier.IdGeneratorI: it maps a natural key to a stable surrogate id in a Go map and resolves ids back to keys.
- `public/identity/identgen/seq` — Package seq provides persistent, per-tag monotonic identifier.IdGeneratorI implementations: each hands out a dense, increasing stream of ids for one tag and ignores the natural key.

### keelson

- `public/keelson/data/chclient` — Package chclient is a HTTP-based ClickHouse client for runtime services per ADR-0026 M2.5b.
- `public/keelson/runtime/agent` — Package agent is the host's side of the app operations contract (ADR-0269): the `runtime.agent.*` services through which a caller — a coordinator running a model's tool loop, or a scene or test holding a test grant — discovers what apps can do and calls their operations on the person's behalf.
- `public/keelson/runtime/agentrun` — Package agentrun is the run journal (ADR-0308): the append-only record a conversation's coordinator writes before every act and the only source of what its model receives.
- `public/keelson/runtime/agentrun/agentrunstore` — Package agentrunstore is the store half of the run journal (ADR-0308 §SD1): two generated record stores on store-owned tables in the house layout — one row per run, latest-wins through the state view, and one row per entry, append-only — in the shape watchbill's tables take (ADR-0223 §SD1, ADR-0105 D3a).
- `public/keelson/runtime/agentrun/agentrunstore/journallaws` — Package journallaws is the journal's laws as SQL over the journal views (journalviews): the queries the integration lane runs against a journal written to a server, where the in-process checks of keelson('evidence_checks') read a store (ADR-0309 §SD6, ADR-0311 §SD8, ADR-0316 §SD4).
- `public/keelson/runtime/agentrun/agentrunstore/journalviews` — Package journalviews composes read-only ClickHouse views over the run journal's ledger (ADR-0308, update of 2026-10-13): one row per run as it stands, and one row per entry at its newest revision — every run, not the newest the keelson tables are bounded to.
- `public/keelson/runtime/agentrun/projection` — Package projection turns a run's journal prefix into the model's request (ADR-0309): a pipeline of passes over the entries — the latest prompt section per name in the profile's declared order, the latest compaction cut with its summary, the latest edit per target, then the message entries from the cut on — returning one row per message with its provenance and label, never a wire string (§SD3).
- `public/keelson/runtime/appcenter/launchcfg` — Package launchcfg is the app center's launch configuration (ADR-0260 §SD1): the leeway-declared DTO a launch request carries (ADR-0135) — the app whose page the window opens on, or the Running tab's filter.
- `public/keelson/runtime/audioout` — Package audioout is the runtime's audio-output capability (ADR-0372 §SD1 and §SD2): an app asks the host for an output over a source and is handed a github.com/stergiotis/boxer/public/science/audio/sink.SinkI; the host binary decides what device is behind it.
- `public/keelson/runtime/audioout/nowplaying` — Package nowplaying is the one recording a window plays: a WAVE file's bytes, loaded and opened off the frame, played through the output the host gives (ADR-0372), with the state a face reads once per frame.
- `public/keelson/runtime/cell` — Package cell is the declared security boundary of a deployment (ADR-0307 §SD1) and the exits across it (ADR-0312): what is inside the cell — this host, its engines, the model hosts the deployment trusts — and, derived from that, every edge boxer mediates that leaves it, a sink with a clearance in TLP terms.
- `public/keelson/runtime/externaledit/launchcfg` — Package launchcfg is the launch configuration that opens an editor on a handed-over text: the leeway-declared DTO a launch request carries.
- `public/keelson/runtime/harness` — Package harness holds the composition shapes an agent harness's seams declare (ADR-0310 §SD1, ADR-0310 §SD11 step 5): a chain runs its elements in declared order, never registration order; a first claim stops at the first element that answers; a guard combines its elements' decisions by maximum, so no element can lower another's and an error is the strongest refusal; a slot holds exactly one provider or a declared default; a registry refuses a duplicate id.
- `public/keelson/runtime/help` — Package help is the runtime's inline-help index.
- `public/keelson/runtime/hostboot` — Package hostboot is the reusable runtime bootstrap for hosts that run keelson apps in the window host (ADR-0211).
- `public/keelson/runtime/introspect` — Package introspect exposes keelson runtime state as Apache Arrow tables that ClickHouse can query (ADR-0094).
- `public/keelson/runtime/introspect/docsearchsql` — Package docsearchsql is the nanopass pass that expands the docsearch('<query>') table-function macro into the documentation search over the section-grained corpora (ADR-0164 §SD5): a UNION of keelson('helpsections'), keelson('adrsections') and the executing server's own system.documentation, scored with the same field weights as the embedded tier (help/search) so a query means the same thing on both.
- `public/keelson/runtime/introspect/introspectengine` — Package introspectengine runs SQL against the keelson introspection tables in-process (ADR-0094 §SD4).
- `public/keelson/runtime/introspect/introspecthost` — Package introspecthost is the in-process start hook for the keelson introspection tables (ADR-0094 §SD3/§SD4).
- `public/keelson/runtime/introspect/introspecthttp` — Package introspecthttp serves keelson introspection tables as Arrow over HTTP, so a clickhouse-local or clickhouse-server can pull them via the url() table function and JOIN them with other data (ADR-0094 §SD3).
- `public/keelson/runtime/introspect/keelsonquery` — Package keelsonquery is the bus side of the introspection tables (ADR-0253): the `keelson.query.<table>` request/reply family an app reads a `keelson()` table through, and the service that answers it over the in-process engine (ADR-0094 §SD4).
- `public/keelson/runtime/introspect/keelsonsql` — Package keelsonsql is a nanopass pass that expands the keelson('<table>') table-function macro into a concrete table source (ADR-0094 §SD4).
- `public/keelson/runtime/introspect/providers` — Package providers implements the GUI-free introspection table providers — env, apps, build, sbom (ADR-0094 §SD8), sql_passes (ADR-0108 §SD5), extbin (ADR-0118), adr/subtask/coderef/adrcontent (ADR-0122 §SD4), helpsections/adrsections (ADR-0164 §SD5), capability/capsection/caprelation (ADR-0168 §SD8), panel_shapes (ADR-0170 §SD5) — and registers them into an introspect.Registry.
- `public/keelson/runtime/introspect/providersgodep` — Package providersgodep exposes this module's Go package graph as keelson introspection tables — `go_packages`, `go_imports`, `go_collection` and `go_package_props` — so the dependency questions ADR-0064 answers inside one app can be asked in SQL, and joined with the rest of the repository corpus (`keelson('adr')`, `keelson('coderef')`, `keelson('sbom')`).
- `public/keelson/runtime/introspect/providersgui` — Package providersgui implements the GUI-coupled v1 introspection providers — demos, windows (ADR-0094 §SD8) and frame times (ADR-0261).
- `public/keelson/runtime/introspect/trivialsql` — Package trivialsql answers the SQL that needs no engine: a keelson table read whole, with or without named arguments, and inline constants (ADR-0290 §SD3).
- `public/keelson/runtime/llm` — Package llm is model inference as a keelson capability (ADR-0254): the `llm.<verb>` request/reply family an app sends text to a model through, and the host-side service that answers it over the repository's one chat-completion client.
- `public/keelson/runtime/llm/promptbook` — Package promptbook is the transformation book (ADR-0216 §SD2, lifted for ADR-0254 §SD6): a corpus of markdown documents whose body IS the system prompt and whose frontmatter is the descriptor, parsed to zero errors by a gate test, and extensible without a rebuild through Register.
- `public/keelson/runtime/llm/ration` — Package ration is the metering and admission core of the model service (ADR-0300): the accounts a call is charged to, the usage it is charged with, the rules a moderator writes over them, and the ledger that checks a call against those rules before it reaches the provider.
- `public/keelson/runtime/llm/tokenmeter` — Package tokenmeter is the one estimate of how many tokens a request takes (ADR-0310 §SD5): anchored on the provider's reported usage where a call reported one, and bytes over four with a flat allowance per image where none did.
- `public/keelson/runtime/moderator` — Package moderator is the host's built-in moderator (ADR-0302): it reads the model service's call events and the agent dispatcher's action records, raises signals that tell a loop from work, and moves each window up a fixed ladder — note, slow, stop — through the levers ADR-0300 provides.
- `public/keelson/runtime/natsbus` — Package natsbus is an app.BusI backed by a NATS core connection — the cross-process transport for the metric plane (ADR-0090 P3) and, more broadly, the post-M4 transport of ADR-0026 §SD4: an external NATS server, with boxer as a client (the server is not embedded or supervised here).
- `public/keelson/runtime/queryengine` — Package queryengine is the engine-adapter contract of [ADR-0144]: the roles an execution engine plays in a query system assembled from the toolbelt, and the types those roles exchange.
- `public/keelson/runtime/queryengine/chlocal` — Package chlocal delivers query results from the chlocal broker ([ADR-0028]) as a runstream — engine 1 of [ADR-0144]'s three, and the one that has the least.
- `public/keelson/runtime/queryengine/chserver` — Package chserver delivers query results from a ClickHouse server over the synchronous HTTP interface — engine 2 of [ADR-0144]'s three, and the only one that plays all three roles.
- `public/keelson/runtime/runstream` — Package runstream is the result-frame contract of a query run (the E3 extension point of doc/explanation/query-system-requirements.md).
- `public/keelson/runtime/schemacheck` — Package schemacheck is the one schema check a process runs over the stored tables it uses (ADR-0387): each table's live columns and stamp are judged against the columns the binary was generated for, the verdicts are kept on a board an operator reads as keelson('schema_tables'), and every table whose verdict is not ok gets one log line.
- `public/keelson/runtime/sealed` — Package sealed holds bytes that must not outlive the process that wrote them (ADR-0240 §SD1).
- `public/keelson/runtime/servicehost` — Package servicehost mounts headless apps — services — at boot and stops them at shutdown (ADR-0352).
- `public/keelson/runtime/sysmetricsbus` — Package sysmetricsbus carries system-metrics snapshots over a bus as a unidirectional publish/subscribe data plane (ADR-0090).
- `public/keelson/runtime/sysmfacts` — Package sysmfacts holds the component DTOs that model a system-metrics sample as `boxer.facts` rows, and (from ADR-0184 M3) the record store generated over them.
- `public/keelson/runtime/sysmreplay` — Package sysmreplay reads stored system-metrics history back out of `boxer.facts` as [sysmsnap.BundleSnapshot] values — the inverse of github.com/stergiotis/boxer/public/keelson/runtime/sysmtee.
- `public/keelson/runtime/sysmscrape` — Package sysmscrape is the scraper-side glue of the system-metrics plane: it wires the /proc- and /sys-reading collectors (public/observability/sysmetrics) to a sysmetricsbus Producer.
- `public/keelson/runtime/sysmtee` — Package sysmtee writes the system-metrics plane into `boxer.facts`.
- `public/keelson/runtime/sysmvocab` — Package sysmvocab is the system-metrics leeway natural-key vocabulary: the memberships that tag a metric sample in `boxer.facts` (ADR-0184 §SD4).
- `public/keelson/runtime/trailviewer/launchcfg` — Package launchcfg is the trail viewer's launch configuration (ADR-0350, proposed): the leeway-declared DTO a launch request carries (ADR-0135) — the case the window opens on, and optionally its time window, its tab and a saved view.
- `public/keelson/runtime/windowhost` — Package windowhost is the M3 multi-app host.
- `public/keelson/runtime/windowopen` — Package windowopen is the client half of the window host's open and raise services: the subjects and the request helpers an app calls to open another app's window or raise one of its own.
- `public/keelson/runtime/workstatelet` — Package workstatelet holds the workstatelet document (ADR-0369): one markdown file that lists windows to open and, optionally, the desktop layout they take.

- `public/llm/openaichat` — Package openaichat is an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions client.

### observability

- `public/observability`
- `public/observability/coverage`
- `public/observability/coverage/covsnap` — Package covsnap holds the pure-data model of Go coverage (ADR-0169 §SD2/§SD3): the decoded meta-data and counter snapshots, and the sampler's pre-aggregated emission model.
- `public/observability/goruntime` — Package goruntime reads the running process's own Go runtime metrics (runtime/metrics) into a caller-owned [Snapshot].
- `public/observability/humanfmt` — Package humanfmt renders metric quantities as compact human-readable strings for the runtime-dashboard apps (imzrt, imztop), which each previously carried a verbatim copy of Bytes (ADR-0061 SD13, same rationale as the SlidingWindow lift).
- `public/observability/logging`
- `public/observability/profiling` — Package profiling wires runtime/pprof's file-based capture into a CLI: --pprofCpuOutputFile starts a CPU profile when the flag is parsed, and ProfilingHandleExit stops it — which is where runtime/pprof serialises the profile, so a host that forgets the exit hook writes an unreadable file.
- `public/observability/profiling/pprofarrow` — Package pprofarrow converts pprof profiles (profile.proto, as written by runtime/pprof or served by net/http/pprof) into a flat Arrow table designed for SQL exploration — the O1 shape of doc/adr-background-work/pprof-profiles-as-data.md.
- `public/observability/profiling/pprofhttp` — Package pprofhttp serves net/http/pprof's handlers on a listener of its own: --pprofHttpListenAddress starts one in the background and the process keeps running.
- `public/observability/slidingwindow` — Package slidingwindow provides a fixed-capacity, drop-oldest ring buffer used by the runtime-dashboard samplers (imzrt, imztop) to retain a bounded history of per-tick metric values for plotting.
- `public/observability/sysmetrics` — Package sysmetrics is the entry point for the Linux system metrics collector tree.
- `public/observability/sysmetrics/battery` — Package battery samples battery and AC-adapter state from /sys/class/power_supply.
- `public/observability/sysmetrics/container` — Package container detects which (if any) container runtime hosts the current process, exposing a typed [EngineE] plus an optional Detail string for runtimes that publish a free-form identifier (e.g.
- `public/observability/sysmetrics/cpu` — Package cpu samples Linux CPU state — totals, per-core utilization, load averages, frequency, RAPL power, and the cgroup-effective cpuset — into a single [Snapshot] per sample.
- `public/observability/sysmetrics/disk` — Package disk samples filesystem mounts and per-block-device I/O state.
- `public/observability/sysmetrics/gpu` — Package gpu hosts the vendor-neutral GPU types — [Device], [Snapshot], and the [SamplerI] interface — that [sysmetrics.Bundle] wires for cross-vendor consumers.
- `public/observability/sysmetrics/gpu/rocm` — Package rocm samples AMD GPU state via the kernel's amdgpu sysfs surface.
- `public/observability/sysmetrics/mem` — Package mem samples Linux memory statistics from /proc/meminfo and, optionally, the ZFS ARC accounting at /proc/spl/kstat/zfs/arcstats.
- `public/observability/sysmetrics/net` — Package net samples per-interface network statistics — link state, IPv4/IPv6 addresses, MAC, and rx/tx byte counters with derived rates — from /sys/class/net and the standard library's net.Interfaces (a thin wrapper over getifaddrs(3)).
- `public/observability/sysmetrics/proc` — Package proc samples the Linux process table by walking /proc/[pid]/{comm,cmdline,stat,statm,status,io} and yielding one [Info] per visible process.
- `public/observability/sysmetrics/psi` — Package psi samples Linux Pressure Stall Information (PSI) from /proc/pressure/{cpu,memory,io} — the share of wall-time tasks spent stalled on each resource, averaged over 10/60/300 s windows.
- `public/observability/sysmetrics/sensors` — Package sensors enumerates Linux temperature sensors via the /sys/class/ hwmon subsystem.
- `public/observability/sysmetrics/sockets` — Package sockets samples the host's listening sockets from /proc/net/{tcp,tcp6,udp,udp6,unix} and attributes each to its owning pid via the /proc/[pid]/fd socket-inode walk — the observed-topology listener table of ADR-0126.
- `public/observability/sysmetrics/sysmsnap` — Package sysmsnap holds the system-metrics data types — the per-domain snapshot structs, the [BundleSnapshot] union, the static CPU [Topology], and the [Domain] enum — with no collector code.
- `public/observability/tracing`

### science

- `public/science/audio/decode` — Package decode opens a recording as a [pcm.SourceI] without the caller naming its format (ADR-0208 §SD5): one interface, two decoders, chosen by the file's first bytes.
- `public/science/audio/pcm` — Package pcm is the sample-level contract of the audio subtree (ADR-0208 SD5): a [Format], the positioned frame reader [SourceI] that every decoder implements and every consumer reads through, and two in-memory sources for tests, demos and benchmarks.
- `public/science/audio/peaks` — Package peaks holds the multi-resolution min/max pyramid the waveform player draws (ADR-0208 §SD2) and the sidecar cache file it is written to (§SD4, §SD12).
- `public/science/audio/sink` — Package sink is the playback-transport contract of the audio subtree (ADR-0208 §SD6) together with its device-less implementation.
- `public/science/audio/sink/lanesink` — Package lanesink is the Go end of the audio lane (ADR-0372 §SD4–§SD6 and §SD9): a device whose samples are played somewhere else — by the viewer page of a remote session, or by the page around a browser tab — and reach it as messages.
- `public/science/audio/sink/playout` — Package playout is the part of a device-backed sink that is not the device (ADR-0372 §SD3): the transport state, the cursor into the source, the rate resampler, the gain and the position bookkeeping of ADR-0208 §SD6, over any device that takes interleaved float32 frames.
- `public/science/audio/sink/pulsesink` — Package pulsesink is the device sink of ADR-0208 SD6: a [sink.SinkI] that plays a [pcm.SourceI] through the PulseAudio native protocol in pure Go (jfreymuth/pulse), which is what a PipeWire or PulseAudio desktop serves.
- `public/science/audio/track` — Package track composes one open recording out of the layers below it (ADR-0208 §SD1): a github.com/stergiotis/boxer/public/science/audio/pcm.SourceI to read frames from, a github.com/stergiotis/boxer/public/science/audio/peaks.Pyramid to draw, a github.com/stergiotis/boxer/public/science/audio/sink.SinkI to play through, and the [TimeBase] every shown time derives from.
- `public/science/audio/wavfile` — Package wavfile decodes RIFF/WAVE and RF64/BW64 streams into interleaved float32 frames behind pcm.SourceI, and writes them back out (ADR-0208 §SD1 for the home, §SD5 for the decoder's place among the two decoders).
- `public/science/geo/geodesy` — Package geodesy is the WGS84 datum, Earth-centred Earth-fixed vectors, geodetic positions with ellipsoidal heights, and local east-north-up tangent frames.
- `public/science/geo/grib` — Package grib reads GRIB edition 1 and 2 messages — the format every numerical weather model is published in — without cgo, without a C codec, and without descent from any existing GRIB library (ADR-0292).
- `public/science/geo/grib/aec` — Package aec decodes the CCSDS 121.0-B-3 Adaptive Entropy Coder — the lossless coding GRIB2's data representation template 5.42 wraps (ADR-0292 §R6) — from the standard alone.
- `public/science/geo/grib/jpeg2000` — Package jpeg2000 decodes the JPEG 2000 Part 1 profile that GRIB2 template 5.40 producers emit (ADR-0292 §R6), from ITU-T T.800 alone: one tile, one component, the reversible 5/3 wavelet without quantization, one quality layer, any precinct partition under a resolution-major progression, and code-block style without arithmetic-coder bypass or per-pass termination.
- `public/science/geo/grib/tables` — Package tables carries the WMO's machine-readable GRIB2 code tables, flag tables and template layouts, and the common table of originating centres, as data (ADR-0292 §R8).
- `public/science/geo/h3` — Package h3 provides bulk, Struct-of-Arrays access to Uber H3 hierarchical geospatial indexing.
- `public/science/geo/h3/h3arrow` — Package h3arrow provides zero-copy adapters from the h3 package's Struct-of-Arrays and CSR outputs to arrow-go arrays.
- `public/science/geo/swisstopo`
- `public/science/geo/vectorfield` — Package vectorfield is the data contract through which a renderer reads a gridded two-component vector field — a 10 m wind, an ocean current, the gradient of a scalar — and the first implementation of it, an in-memory pyramid (ADR-0249 SD1, SD2).
- `public/science/geo/vectorfield/gribfield` — Package gribfield reads GRIB wind into the planes a vector field is made of (ADR-0292 SD4): pairs of eastward and northward components on a regular latitude/longitude grid, one pair per valid time, as a keelsonfield.Field.
- `public/science/geo/vectorfield/keelsonfield` — Package keelsonfield serves a gridded vector field held in memory as a family of keelson tables (ADR-0291): the relation itself, its options, and one table per statement purpose of sqlfield, each taking that statement's parameters as named arguments (ADR-0290) and replying in that statement's shape.
- `public/science/geo/vectorfield/sqlfield` — Package sqlfield is a [vectorfield.SourceI] over a field held in ClickHouse (ADR-0250): every window request is one reduction query, so what crosses the wire is bounded by the request and the field may be any size.
- `public/science/imaging` — Package imaging holds an image as measured samples, apart from any way of showing it (ADR-0373 §SD1, §SD2): one to four planes of one size and one sample kind, a colour model that says what the planes are, and the provenance of the whole.
- `public/science/imaging/decode` — Package decode reads a PNG or a JPEG file into an [imaging.Image] without passing its samples through 8 bits or through premultiplied alpha (ADR-0373 §SD10).
- `public/science/imaging/display` — Package display turns an image's samples into the colours a screen shows, under a recipe that is a value of its own (ADR-0373 §SD4, §SD5).
- `public/science/imaging/levels` — Package levels reduces an image by halving, for showing it smaller than it is (ADR-0373 §SD6).
- `public/science/imaging/samples` — Package samples makes a few synthetic images, each computed from its coordinates and so the same on every run and every host: something to show in a demo, to seed a scene with, or to try a display recipe on without a file.
- `public/science/imaging/stats` — Package stats computes numbers about a plane from its samples (ADR-0373 §SD8): a histogram, and from it the range and percentiles of the values.
- `public/science/imaging/tiles` — Package tiles holds an image as tiles and the reduced levels over it (ADR-0374 §SD7): level 0 cut into 512-pixel tiles, and each level a viewer reduces to — means, minima and maxima, exactly as the levels package defines them — cut the same way.

### semistructured

- `public/semistructured/leeway/aspectcodec` — Package aspectcodec implements the v2 aspect-segment codec (ADR-0182 SD1), shared by the three aspect vocabularies.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/base62`
- `public/semistructured/leeway/canonform` — Package canonform computes the leeway canonical record form — ADR-0201 — and the digests over it.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/canonicaltypes` — Package canonicaltypes is the canonical type system leeway columns are declared in: a compact, target-independent spelling of primitive types (`u64`, `f32l`, `s`, `y`, `z64`, `vc`), their homogeneous-array and set forms (`sh`, `u64m`), groups of them, and signatures.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/canonwire` — Package canonwire is the leeway canonical wire generator — ADR-0210: the pieces that read a table description at generation time and emit a per-table encoder and decoder, as opposed to the pieces those emitted classes call at run time.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/canonwire/runtime` — Package runtime is the runtime of the leeway canonical wire — ADR-0210: the pieces a generated per-table encoder or decoder calls, as opposed to the pieces the generator emits.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/canonwire/streamenc` — Package streamenc encodes leeway entities as the canonical wire (ADR-0210) from any Arrow batch a streamreadaccess.Driver can read — no generated per-table classes, only the table description the driver was built with.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/card`
- `public/semistructured/leeway/chpack` — Package chpack defines and installs the co/ragged ClickHouse function pack (ADR-0162): the expression-level leeway query vocabulary, shipped as server-side SQL user-defined functions.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/chviews` — Package chviews declares the leeway schema-decode views (ADR-0226): three ClickHouse views that read a leeway physical column name apart over system.columns and system.tables, so the structure a name carries — section, column, role, canonical type, aspects, row config, co-section and streaming group — is selectable instead of re-derived by hand in every ad-hoc query.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/common` — Package common holds the leeway table model every other stage reads: the table description, the intermediate representation derived from it, and the enumerations that name plain-item lanes, membership channels and column roles.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/constructsql` — Package constructsql is the leeway constructor family of ADR-0181 §SD2: LW_PLAIN, LW_TV, LW_TV_MEMB and LW_TV_SUPPORT as the client-side nanopass expansion pass LwConstructExpand.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/ddl` — Package ddl is the target-independent half of leeway's DDL stage: the naming convention that turns a column's leeway coordinates into a physical column name, and the driver that walks an IntermediateTableRepresentation and asks a target's code generator for each column.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/ddl/arrow`
- `public/semistructured/leeway/ddl/clickhouse`
- `public/semistructured/leeway/dml` — Package dml generates the write side of a leeway table: Go types that append entities, their plain values and their tagged-value sections to Arrow record builders, and hand back finished records.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/encodingaspects` — Code generated by copy paste; DO NOT EDIT.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/jsonshred` — Package jsonshred turns a JSON document into leeway's semi-structured attributes and back: each leaf is a (path, parameters, value) triple in the section of its canonical type, as the leeway-advanced skill's JSON mapping describes, and Compose rebuilds the document from the triples (plan002 B1).
- `public/semistructured/leeway/lwextract` — Package lwextract builds the ClickHouse expression that locates one attribute in a leeway tagged section and extracts its value (ADR-0181 §SD3).
- `public/semistructured/leeway/lwlens` — Package lwlens reads a leeway batch as rows of slots and plans how to draw them under two reader intents: how much the reader cares about structure versus values, and whether each row is drawn on its own terms or on a frame shared across rows.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/lwread` — Package lwread reads leeway records as a person or a model reads them (ADR-0289 §SD3): each record as its attributes, each attribute named by what it is rather than by where it sits, its values spelled once for every reader, and every value the reading leaves out counted.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/lwsql` — Package lwsql bridges leeway physical column names to the nanopass SQL pipeline.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/lwsqlsurface` — Package lwsqlsurface is the entry point to leeway's SQL read surface (ADR-0171): the three server-side function families, declared as one set, installed by one call, and reported by one version marker.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/mapping`
- `public/semistructured/leeway/mappingplan` — Package mappingplan is the schema-agnostic data model of a leeway DTO ↔ codec mapping: the parsed Plan (plain columns + tagged-value fields), the membership-channel enum and its carriage axes, and the canonical→Go derived views on Plan / PlainCol / TaggedField (GoType / IsSlice / IsRoaring, backed by DeriveGoShape).
- `public/semistructured/leeway/marshall/clickhouse/readback`
- `public/semistructured/leeway/marshall/component` — Package component is a catalogue of leeway component kinds and the archetype question over them (ADR-0146 D5).
- `public/semistructured/leeway/marshall/go/marshallgen` — Package marshallgen is the generic Go DTO → leeway codec generator.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/marshall/go/marshallreflect` — Package marshallreflect is the runtime-reflection sibling of boxer/public/semistructured/leeway/marshall/go/marshallgen.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/marshall/lw` — Package lw declares the marker types for the leeway nested-struct marshalling front-end (doc/howto/leeway-marshalling.md).
- `public/semistructured/leeway/marshall/marshalltypes` — Package marshalltypes holds the plain carrier structs for the leeway codec's Cut-2 parametrized / mixed membership channels (ADR-0008 D3).
- `public/semistructured/leeway/membershiprole` — Package membershiprole classifies Leeway memberships as primary or secondary and decides whether their parameters contribute to attribute identity.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/namemint/assignments` — Package assignments reads and writes a name mint's committed assignment golden: the (ordinal, name, id) table a version-controlled vocabulary promises to keep.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/namemint/contract` — Package contract states what a name mint accepts: which tag values a registry may be built on, and which names and machine-readable forms it may register.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/namemint/naturalkey` — Package naturalkey encodes the machine-readable form of a name a mint registers — the deterministic serialization that makes an identity reproducible from its parts rather than assigned by a counter.
- `public/semistructured/leeway/namemint/registry` — Package registry is the name mint: where a name is struck into the id that stands for it on the wire, and where that mapping is held.

### storage

- `public/storage/recordstore/chexec` — Package chexec provides concrete recordstore.ExecutorI implementations.
- `public/storage/recordstore/dimension` — Package dimension is the ADR-0112 slice-S1 runtime: a DimensionStore interns a natural key to a surrogate identifier.TaggedId via an injected identifier.IdGeneratorI, emits a descriptor fact exactly once (on the generator's first-sight "fresh" signal), and resolves an id back to its descriptor.
- `public/storage/recordstore/dimension/actor` — Package actor is the second dimension.Store instance (ADR-0295 §SD8, over ADR-0112): it interns the claimed principal, purpose and app of a call identity to a surrogate id and stores the descriptor once per distinct triple.
- `public/storage/recordstore/dimension/provenance` — Package provenance is the first dimension.Store instance (ADR-0112 SD6): it interns a writer's (host, Go call-stack) to a surrogate id and stores the descriptor — hostname and symbolicated frames — once per distinct stack.
- `public/storage/recordstore/evidence` — Package evidence holds the laws a record store under the evidence profile satisfies, and the hash constructions they are stated over (ADR-0327 §SD1): a chain digest per row over the row's canonical item and its predecessor's digest; a commitment per vaulted component under an opening that is destroyed with the content; a mark that says what an absent component means; heads anchored outside the writer's control.
- `public/storage/recordstore/evidence/anchor` — Package anchor is the anchor store contract below the keelson runtime (ADR-0327 §SD7): the append-only record `(cell, scope, ordinal, scheme, digest)` of chain heads and seals an organisation holds outside any person's control, answered with a receipt, so that a store written on a host the person administers can be checked against heads it cannot rewrite.
- `public/storage/recordstore/evidence/audit` — Package audit holds the audit event below the keelson runtime (ADR-0327 §SD8): the component a domain writes its records of processing with (ADR-0296 §SD1), its bounds, the origin component every row of a recorder carries, the rows a recorder writes about itself ([Invalid], [Gap]), the identity rule every recorder applies ([Stamp], [OriginOf]), and the forwarder seam a carrier adapter implements.
- `public/storage/recordstore/gen` — Package gen is the recordstore generator (ADR-0100 SD6): one invocation takes a leeway TableDesc, a set of component DTO sources and the envelope-role bindings, and emits a complete store package by driving the existing leeway generators (dml, ddl/clickhouse, readaccess, marshallgen) and then emitting the store glue over their output.
- `public/storage/recordstore/ipcexec` — Package ipcexec is the write-only recordstore executor: a generated store pointed at it appends every flushed batch to one Arrow IPC *stream* — the shape `INSERT INTO t FORMAT ArrowStream` loads — instead of a ClickHouse table.
- `public/storage/recordstore/rowcas` — Package rowcas composes the statements of a compare-and-set on one row of a ClickHouse MergeTree table, and carries the conditions under which that is what they are.
- `public/storage/recordstore/schemaplan` — Package schemaplan derives the statements that bring a stored table to the columns its store was generated for, when the change is mechanical (ADR-0387): generated columns the table lacks are added, columns present under an aspect-only variant of their name (ADR-0182) are renamed and given the generated codec, a plain MergeTree table without an insert deduplication window gets one, and the table is stamped with the generating schema.

### streaming

- `public/streaming/persisted/kafka` — Package kafka exposes a franz-go-based Kafka consumer and producer for this repository's persisted-streaming subsystem.
- `public/streaming/stevedore` — Package stevedore is the routing, failure and state handling around an ingestion processor that a streaming framework drives as an external process (ADR-0252).
- `public/streaming/stevedore/deadletter` — Package deadletter is where a stevedore lander or driver records what it gave up on (ADR-0252 §SD3): one row of the stevedoreDeadLetter kind per message or request, through the facts-bound generated store, or a log line where no store is at hand.
- `public/streaming/stevedore/drive` — Package drive runs an application's [stevedore.HandlerI] and [stevedore.SinkI] in one process with no framework and no topic (ADR-0252, Updates 2026-09-23): a source yields requests, each is handled under the same deadline, panic recovery and retry the processor host applies, each item is landed, the sink is flushed, and only then is the checkpoint advanced.
- `public/streaming/stevedore/host` — Package host runs an application's [stevedore.HandlerI] as the external process a streaming framework drives (ADR-0252 §SD2, §SD3): one framed request in on stdin, one reply out, the failure reported the way the framework's processor expects, and the handler bounded in size, time and panics so the framework sees a status rather than a killed process.
- `public/streaming/stevedore/lander` — Package lander consumes stevedore items from a topic and hands them to an application's [stevedore.SinkI] (ADR-0252 §SD5): it decodes each message's envelope, lands each item, and commits the batch's offset only after the sink's flush returned.
- `public/streaming/stevedore/stevedorefacts` — Package stevedorefacts is the facts-bound record store for what a stevedore lander writes on its own account (ADR-0252 §SD3, §SD5): the dead-letter kind, one row per message given up on.
- `public/streaming/stevedore/stevedoreitem` — Package stevedoreitem is the leeway-coded wire form of the stevedore item envelope (ADR-0252 §SD2): what one message of a fan-out carries beside the application's payload.
- `public/streaming/stevedore/stevedorevocab` — Package stevedorevocab is the stevedore leeway natural-key vocabulary: the memberships of the item envelope that crosses a pipeline (ADR-0252 §SD2) and of the dead-letter row a lander writes (ADR-0252 §SD3).
- `public/streaming/stevedore/wire` — Package wire is the framing half of the stevedore contract (ADR-0252 §SD2): how one message crosses a pipe to an external-process processor, and how several parts travel inside one message.

### thestack

- `public/thestack/imzero2/browserhost` — Package browserhost is the Go side of imzero2 in a browser tab (ADR-0263): the pieces a wasip1 module needs to be a keelson host inside a Web Worker, with the Rust browser host (rust/imzero2/browser) beside it and the existing viewer page painting the mesh.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/browserhost/tabhost` — Package tabhost is a browser-tab binary's body as a library (ADR-0278 SD1, proposed): the program that mounts one registered keelson app on an in-process bus, runs it as a wasip1 reactor inside the page's worker (ADR-0263), runs the same app natively against a client binary over the pipe, builds a bundle and serves one, and reports what its apps declare that a tab does not serve.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/browserhost/web` — Package web is what the page loads beside the two wasm modules: the worker that runs them and the WASI shim between them (ADR-0263), plus the viewer page itself, gathered so a server can hand all three out of the binary that serves the bundle (ADR-0278 SD3).
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/bgjobrow` — Package bgjobrow draws a running bgjob as the standard job row — bar, share and time left, the job's note, Cancel — and cancels the job when Cancel is clicked.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/boxenplot` — Package boxenplot is a painter helper (ADR-0267) for letter-value (Hofmann, Wickham & Kafadar 2017) plots.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/canonicaltypeedit` — Package canonicaltypeedit is an immediate-mode widget (ADR-0267): an editor for a single primitive leeway canonical type ([canonicaltypes]), and for a signature of them.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/canonicaltypesummary` — Package canonicaltypesummary is an immediate-mode widget (ADR-0267): a tethered value-inspector for a single leeway canonical type ([canonicaltypes]).
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/componentview` — Package componentview is an immediate-mode widget (ADR-0267), the typed per-component complement to the generic leewaywidgets.RecordCard (ADR-0075).
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/distsummary` — Package distsummary is an immediate-mode widget (ADR-0267) summarising a single statistical distribution on two levels.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/ecdf` — Package ecdf is a painter helper (ADR-0267) for plotting an empirical CDF together with a finite-sample exact simultaneous confidence band (Berk-Jones by default; DKW / equal-precision / higher-criticism available per the underlying ecdfbands library).
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/filepicker` — Package filepicker is a semi-retained imzero2 widget (ADR-0267): an in-app file open / save / pick-folder dialog rendered as an egui::Window.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/fsbrowser` — Package fsbrowser renders any io/fs.FS as a file browser: one directory at a time as a sortable list, or the tree below the current directory as an outline, with a breadcrumb above, a quick filter, a selection, a keyboard cursor, and host-supplied columns beside name, size and modification time (ADR-0200 §SD2).
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/glossview` — Package glossview draws gloss faces: a value's inline face in its tone, a gloss/url value as a link, and a column's resolution as hover text.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/imageview` — Package imageview is a semi-retained widget (ADR-0267) that shows an [imaging.Image] through a [display.Recipe] (ADR-0373 §SD7): pan, zoom, a readout of the pixel under the pointer, and a colour bar for a single plane.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/impacttolerance` — Package impacttolerance is an immediate-mode widget (ADR-0267) that draws important business services against their impact tolerances under named scenarios — the operational-resilience chart.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/implot` — Package implot is a Go port of the core of ImPlot (https://github.com/epezent/implot, MIT, © 2020 Evan Pezent), re-targeted from Dear ImGui's draw list onto the imzero2 painter lane (ADR-0149).
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/jobprogress` — Package jobprogress is a small immediate-mode widget (ADR-0267) that renders the progress of a background job — an optional title, a progress bar, and a humanized "47% · 1.2 k rows/s · 2m05s left" status line with an optional Cancel button — for embedding inline beneath (or beside) the thing the job is computing (e.g.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/kanban` — Package kanban is an immediate-mode imzero2 widget (ADR-0267) that renders a board of columns and the cards in them, and lets the user move a card between columns (and reorder it within a column) with per-card controls.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/leewaywidgets`
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/mappingplanview` — Package mappingplanview is a semi-retained imzero2 widget (ADR-0267) for authoring a leeway mappingplan spec and live-previewing the code it compiles to: a [View] built once with [New] draws a host-owned [Model] every frame.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/metricsoverlay` — Package metricsoverlay is an immediate-mode widget (ADR-0267) rendering frame-timing readouts for embedding in a menu or status bar.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/notebookcells` — Package notebookcells registers renderers of a notebook's presentation cells that are drawn small, for a report read among prose: `marks`, the instants and intervals of a few things on one time axis, and `points`, places on a map.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/notebookview` — Package notebookview is a semi-retained widget (ADR-0267) that draws a notebook: a markdown document of typed cells with the blobs it names (ADR-0371).
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/portolan/flowoverlay` — Package flowoverlay draws a gridded vector field — wind, a current — on a portolan map as particles drifting along it, each trailing a short fading stroke (ADR-0249).
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/portolan/h3overlay` — Package h3overlay draws H3 cells on a portolan map: cell fills from the cells' boundaries, a region's outline from their dissolve, both computed through the h3 wasm bridge (public/science/geo/h3), which the map widget itself does not depend on — only a caller that wants H3 pays for the runtime.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/recordtable` — Package recordtable draws an Arrow record as an egui_table grid: an immediate-mode widget (ADR-0267), [RenderGrid], and the two parts it is built from, which a host with a grid of its own uses directly.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/regexsummary` — Package regexsummary is an immediate-mode widget (ADR-0267): a two-level summary of a single regular-expression value.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/riskmatrix` — Package riskmatrix is an immediate-mode widget (ADR-0267) that draws a risk register as a likelihood × impact matrix.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/schemaview` — Package schemaview is an imzero2 widget that renders a leeway schema — a [common.TableDesc] — as a master-detail inspector across two dock panes: a collapsible section navigator ("structure") and a decoded property pane ("detail").
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/sqleditor` — Package sqleditor is the imzero2 SQL editing surface: a no-wrap monospace [c.TextEdit] with a line-number gutter and marks lane beside it, lexical and semantic syntax colour, a sparse overlay channel for the embedder's own decorations, and multi-statement awareness (which statement the caret is in, and what a run-under-cursor would ship).
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/taskmonitor` — Package taskmonitor is a semi-retained imzero2 widget (ADR-0267), the M4 of ADR-0038: it observes task.> over the bus and renders an in-flight list (with progress bar + per-row cancel button) and a rolling history of finished tasks.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/trendsmooth` — Package trendsmooth is the shared modified-sinc smoothing overlay for the monitoring apps' trend plots — the app-consumer surface of github.com/stergiotis/boxer/public/analytics/timeseries/mssmooth (ADR-0152).
- `public/thestack/imzero2/egui2/widgets/waveform` — Package waveform is the audio waveform player of ADR-0208, a semi-retained widget in the sense of ADR-0267: the waveform of a [track.Track] drawn on the painter lane with a playhead, click-to-seek, drag-to-pan, wheel and pinch zoom, a duration ruler and a hover readout.
- `public/thestack/imzero2/hostmain` — Package hostmain is the imzero2 host binary's body as a library: the command tree of the desktop and headless host — the `imzero2` group with `demo`, `drive` and `scene`, the observability and watchbill commands — with the logging, profiling, tracing, debugger and coverage flags, and the exit hooks that flush them.
